key_insight: FERPO improves continuous-control policies by fitting an actor to a forward-KL target distribution derived from critic values, avoiding unstable action-gradient backpropagation through the critic.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical on-policy RL alternative that can yield more reliable policy updates, better exploration over multiple good actions, and faster actor optimization in robotics/control tasks.
method: Derive an optimal action distribution from a policy-improvement objective with entropy and KL regularization.
Estimate the forward-KL actor loss using self-normalized importance sampling over actions from the rollout policy.
Keep the target close to the rollout policy to stabilize importance weights and reduce update variance.
evidence_signal: The paper reports competitive performance and sample-efficiency gains on MuJoCo Playground and ManiSkill, plus faster actor updates than REPPO in computational benchmarks.
watch_item: Forward-KL fitting depends on well-behaved importance weights, so performance may degrade if the target distribution drifts too far from the rollout policy or SNIS estimates become high variance.
